title: Freeze contracts, reserve guard, and the synthetic-fleet generator
inputs: Brief dataclasses. health is remaining capacity fraction. age() returns capacity fraction lost over dt_s.
accept: pytest tests/test_contracts.py passes. The guard rejects any setpoint whose energy would enter reserve. allocate, step_thermal, and age match the brief signatures. Fleet seed 7 is deterministic, tagged synthetic, and uses 20 kW / 39.2 kWh. Default reserve_frac 0.30 and replacement health 0.70 are labeled assumptions in the module docstring.
risk: Any later edit to these fields invalidates the worktrees. Changes require all owners before dependent tasks resume.

title: Lumped enclosure thermal model
inputs: sun_exposure, ambient C, power kW, dt seconds. Heat terms are ambient exchange, solar gain, and resistive heating.
accept: Zero power and zero sun converges to ambient within 0.1 C. Steady temperature rises with power and with sun_exposure. A steady-state energy-balance residual test passes.
risk: A sign error on solar gain or resistive heating reverses the product. Monotonic tests are merge blockers.

title: Cache ERCOT 2025 and weather as Parquet
inputs: gridstatus 2025 system load, load forecasts, real-time prices by load zone, and published 4CP intervals. Hourly weather for Austin, Seguin, and Denton.
accept: python -m runway.ingest --offline exits 0 with the network disabled and matches manifest.json. The fixture slice alone can build the June published-interval call.
risk: APIs throttle. Commit the first good pull as the fixture before any other data work.

title: Allocator with hard limits and a pluggable marginal-cost callback
inputs: Call, UnitState list, cost callback. Water-fill on marginal cost with box constraints.
accept: Each setpoint stays at or above reserve; power is inside [0, p_max_kw]; setpoint power plus shortfall_kw equals requested kW within 1e-6; shortfall_kw >= 0; outputs are deterministic. If available power is below the request, shortfall equals the gap and no reserve energy is used. The stub cost does not import aging.
risk: Water-fill fills a shortfall from reserve. Property tests are merge blockers.

title: Async workers with injected faults and a local reserve refusal
inputs: Contracts, reserve guard. Faults: offline, derated, stale telemetry, under-delivery.
accept: Each fault changes telemetry the dispatcher reads. An illegal setpoint is still refused at the worker. Tests pass offline.
risk: Fault flags never reach the dispatcher. The test goes through emitted telemetry.

title: LFP aging model, BLAST-Lite band, three assumption sets
inputs: In-repo BLAST-Lite LFP reference. Arrhenius calendar and cycle terms, a C-rate term, a cold-charge penalty. Files: nominal, low_sensitivity, high_sensitivity.
accept: Relative error versus BLAST-Lite at a precommitted reference is inside a precommitted band. A hotter enclosure loses more capacity. Cold-charge is inactive above the temperature named in the file. Swapping JSON changes the loss and leaves the function body unchanged.
risk: BLAST-Lite overruns six hours. Ship the nominal algebraic model, mark the overlay failed, and expect a lower technical-depth score.

title: Thin end-to-end run on the published June 2025 interval
inputs: June 2025 published 4CP fixture, 32 synthetic units, seed 7.
accept: Network disabled, the command prints one call_id, 32 setpoints, and shortfall_kw >= 0. JSON header has synthetic=true. This ships while T07 is still open.
risk: Ingest slips past the quarter. The committed fixture is what this command reads.

title: Pre-register the hunting rule and score 2025 candidate calls
inputs: CALLING_RULE.md committed first. A Chicago calendar day in Jun-Sep 2025 is a candidate when its max day-ahead system forecast is at least 0.97 times the max daily day-ahead peak from the first of that month through that day. One 90-minute call centered on the forecast peak, source 4cp_candidate, utility Austin Energy. peak_odds is that ratio clipped to [0,1]. A hit means a published 4CP timestamp falls inside the window. System-load proxy is written in the file.
accept: The rule commit is an ancestor of the output commit. hit_flags.json carries a hash of the rule. Every Jun-Sep 2025 published 4CP timestamp is a hit or has a miss_reason. CI fails if 0.97 changes after hit_flags.json exists. The 0.96 and 0.98 counts may appear only as a pair in a side file.
risk: Retuning 0.97 after seeing official dates. The hash gate blocks that.

title: Wire marginal wear from age composed with step_thermal
inputs: age(), step_thermal(), allocate callback. Glide path is linear from health 1.0 at age 0 to 0.70 at term_years. Delivery-risk multiplier is 2 when telemetry is older than 15 minutes and peak_odds >= 0.9. Both are assumptions.
accept: Higher sun_exposure receives weakly less power at equal SOC. The unit further below its glide path receives weakly less power. A test fails if the cost module is not marginal.py. On n<=16 the objective gap versus SLSQP is printed and a gap above 1% fails.
risk: A non-convex finite difference makes lambda search oscillate. Use a damped search and keep the SLSQP gap test.

title: Dispatcher journal, re-solve, and real subprocess restart
inputs: Workers, allocate, append-only journal. Live fault: offline the 15% of units with the largest setpoints. Scale ladder: 4000, 2000, 500. MW scales as 40 * N / 4000.
accept: Seeded wave has reserve_violations 0, a new seq, and metrics for tracking_error_kw, shortfall_kw, and resole_latency_ms. Latency is wall-clock. Killing the dispatcher subprocess and restarting applies each seq once. Live demo N is the largest ladder step whose re-solve p50 is under 1000 ms.
risk: 4000 actors miss the latency budget. The ladder is the mitigation and N must be on screen.

title: Benchmark allocate at 1k, 10k, and 100k units
accept: Prints p50 milliseconds at 1000, 10000, and 100000 units. The timer wraps allocate() and excludes fleet generation. No workers start. CPU model is recorded.
risk: The timer includes setup and the number is useless on camera.

title: Local dashboard bound to pipeline JSON
inputs: Port four prototype views: thermal fleet, water-fill, heat curve, replay.
accept: Loads with the network off. The hosted artifact URL is absent from the repo. The DOM contains 'synthetic fleet'. Editing the fixture hero number changes the page.
risk: The port becomes a redesign. Four views only.

title: Hero wear ratio on misses versus hits, under even spread
inputs: Candidate calls, Austin ambient, even spread, three assumption sets, 4000 synthetic units, 40 MW. Each call starts at SOC 1.0. Both fleet size and initial SOC are assumptions. Even spread authors the hero.
accept: Contains wear_per_kwh_miss, wear_per_kwh_hit, ratio, and wear_fraction_on_misses for even spread on all three sets, plus total wear for runway, even_spread, and most_charge_first. Same seed is byte-identical. A ratio near 1.0 is a valid result and does not authorize a rule edit.
risk: The ratio collapses to a day count. Wear per kWh is the check.

title: Season replay, feasible-policy comparison, saturation row, over-call caveat
inputs: Summer 2025 calls. Policies share the reserve guard: Runway, even spread, most-charge-first (highest SOC at call start, unit_id tie-break). Fleets: 4000 units at 40 MW, and 2000 units at 40 MW. Repeating 2025 across a contract term must be labeled as a repeated year.
accept: Seed 7 is byte-identical. Reserve violations are 0. If any policy shortfalls on the 4000-unit base calls, lower MW until all three have zero shortfall and compare early replacements only there. The 2000-unit row records shortfall by policy. The over-call fixture shows early replacements for all three. The JSON includes ranking_flipped_across_assumption_sets.
risk: Most-charge-first loses only because it is energy-infeasible. The feasible-MW gate stops that false win.

title: Bind the demo entrypoint to the chaos-test seed
accept: Pre-fault setpoints match the chaos test. The command runs offline and writes the same metrics fields.
risk: A second video-only path appears. Review blocks any entrypoint that does not call the dispatcher under test.

title: 12CP counterfactual count table
inputs: Same hunting score, all twelve months of 2025, 30-minute window. Dollars only from the brief: about $17/kW per 4CP interval and $5.70/kW under 12CP, labeled rough and ERCOT-wide.
accept: Counts are code-generated. The file is labeled a counterfactual on a proposed rule whose decision is expected December 2026. No wear model.
risk: It crowds the data owner during the hero report. Drop it first if T09 slips.

title: One-command demo, decision table, fallback recording, citation script
outputs: README quickstart, VIDEO_SCRIPT.md, outputs/demo/decision_table.csv, fallback recording
accept: A clean venv finishes the README command offline. The CSV has unit_id, power_kw, enclosure_c, marginal_wear, and assignment for units whose setpoint changed on the re-solve. Every spoken number cites a file or a brief figure. The recording uses seed 7. Record the fault beat when T12 is green and add the hero chart when T09 is green.
risk: Recording waits on the full replay. Split it as the accept text says.
